title: Middle school math: equations
description: Grade 7 algebra foundations — letters, expressions, balance and linear equations, with an interactive balance world.
assumptions: Learner can compute with negative numbers and understands multiplication and division. No algebra background is assumed.
stage.1.title: Letters and balance
stage.1.goal: Read algebraic expressions, evaluate by substitution, and state the balance rule.
stage.2.title: Linear equations
stage.2.goal: Solve one-step and two-step equations and model stories with equations.
variables.title: Letters stand for numbers
variables.goal: Read and write simple algebraic expressions.
variables.reading: A letter can stand for a number we do not know yet. 3a means 3 × a, not 3 + a. If a = 4, then 3a = 12. a + a + a is also 3a because it is three copies of a joined by addition. The number in front of a letter is called its coefficient.
variables.exercise: Pick a number for a between 1 and 9. Write 3a, a + a + a and 3 + a, compute all three, and explain which two must always match and why.
variables.rubric: You read 3a as multiplication, evaluate it for a chosen value, and explain why 3 + a is different.
variables.q1.a.fb: Right: the coefficient multiplies the letter.
variables.q1.b.fb: The number in front multiplies; it is not added.
expressions.title: Evaluate expressions by substitution
expressions.goal: Substitute a value and follow the order of operations.
expressions.reading: To evaluate 2x + 5 when x = 4, replace x with 4 first: 2 × 4 + 5. Multiplication comes before addition, so 8 + 5 = 13. Writing 245 joins digits instead of computing; writing 11 adds 2 + 4 + 5 and ignores the coefficient. Substitution is replacement, not concatenation.
expressions.exercise: Evaluate 2x + 5 for x = 1, 4 and 10. Make a small table. Then find the x that makes 2x + 5 equal to 21 and check it.
expressions.rubric: You substitute correctly, multiply before adding, and check a value by putting it back.
expressions.q1.b.fb: That joins digits; substitution means replace and compute.
expressions.q1.hint.1: Replace x with 4, then multiply first.
equation-balance.title: Equations are balances
equation-balance.goal: Keep an equation balanced by doing the same thing to both sides.
equation-balance.reading: An equation is a balance: x + 3 = 7 says the left pan equals the right pan. Take 3 from the left only and the balance breaks. Take 3 from BOTH sides and it stays balanced: x = 4. Whatever you do to one side — add, subtract, multiply or divide by a nonzero number — do to the other side too.
equation-balance.exercise: Use the balance world: set left 7, right 7, then change only one side and observe. Write the rule you discovered in one sentence.
equation-balance.rubric: You state the same-operation-on-both-sides rule and demonstrate it with the balance.
equation-balance.q1.q: To solve x + 3 = 7, what keeps the balance?
equation-balance.q1.a.fb: Right: the same operation on both sides keeps equality.
equation-balance.q1.b: Subtract 3 from the left side only.
equation-balance.q1.b.fb: Changing one side alone breaks the balance.
solve-one-step.title: Solve one-step equations
solve-one-step.goal: Undo one operation using the balance rule.
solve-one-step.reading: 3x = 12 asks: three copies of x balance 12. Divide BOTH sides by 3: x = 4. Check by putting 4 back: 3 × 4 = 12. Multiplying 12 by 3 gives 36, which solves nothing; subtracting 3 gives 9 and confuses the coefficient with an added number.
solve-one-step.exercise: Solve 5x = 35 and x ÷ 2 = 6. Check each answer by substitution. Write which operation undoes which.
solve-one-step.rubric: You apply the inverse operation to both sides and verify by substitution.
solve-one-step.q1.a.fb: Right: divide both sides by 3; 3 × 4 = 12 checks out.
solve-one-step.q1.b.fb: That multiplies 12 by 3 instead of undoing the coefficient.
solve-one-step.q1.hint.1: Undo multiplication with division on both sides.
solve-two-step.title: Solve two-step equations
solve-two-step.reading: 2x + 5 = 13 has two operations on x. Undo the +5 first: subtract 5 from both sides, 2x = 8. Then divide both sides by 2: x = 4. Check: 2 × 4 + 5 = 13. Undoing in the wrong order — dividing 13 by 2 first — leaves the +5 behind and gives a wrong answer.
solve-two-step.exercise: Solve 3x − 4 = 11 and 4x + 7 = 31. Check both. Compare with your struggle attempt: which step differed?
solve-two-step.rubric: You undo operations in reverse order, keep both sides balanced, and check by substitution.
solve-two-step.struggle: Before reading: solve 3x − 4 = 11 on your own. Write every step and where you get stuck. Keep your first attempt even if the check fails.
solve-two-step.q1.a.fb: Right: subtract 5 from both sides, then divide by 2; the check passes.
solve-two-step.q1.b.fb: That adds 5 instead of subtracting it from both sides.
word-to-equation.title: Turn stories into equations
word-to-equation.goal: Model a story with an equation, solve it, and check reasonableness.
word-to-equation.reading: "A number doubled, plus 5, gives 13" becomes 2x + 5 = 13: doubled is 2x, plus 5 is +5, gives is =. 2(x + 5) = 13 would mean "add 5 first, then double" — a different story. After solving x = 4, ask: does double 4 plus 5 give 13? Yes. The equation, the solution and the story must all agree.
word-to-equation.exercise: Write your own number story for 3x − 4 = 11, solve it, and check the answer against your story. Trade with someone and check each other.
word-to-equation.rubric: You translate the story faithfully, solve with balanced steps, and check the answer in the original story.
word-to-equation.q1.q: Which equation matches "a number doubled, plus 5, gives 13"?
word-to-equation.q1.b.fb: That adds 5 first and then doubles — a different story.
word-to-equation.q1.hint.1: Follow the order of the words.
expressions.s1.content: To evaluate 2x + 5 at x = 4: replace x with 4 to get 2 × 4 + 5. Multiply first: 8 + 5 = 13.
expressions.s1.prompt: In your own words: why multiply before adding?
expressions.s1.fb: Right — the coefficient multiplies x first; addition comes after.
expressions.s1.hint: 2x means 2 times x, so that happens first.
expressions.s2.prompt: When x = 3, match each expression to its value.
expressions.s2.hint: Substitute 3 for x in each expression.
expressions.s3.hint: Replace x with 4, then multiply before adding.
expressions.s4.a.fb: That is 3 × 2 only; do not forget the +1.
expressions.evaluate.scaffold: After replacing x with 4 you have 2 × 4 + 5. Compute 2 × 4 first, then add 5 — do not add 4 + 5 first.
variables.worked.prompt: In your own words: why are 3a and 3 + a different?
variables.worked.content: 3a means 3 × a. If a = 4, then 3a = 12. a + a + a is also 3a.
variables.evaluate-3a.scaffold: 3a means 3 × a. Replace a with 5 and compute 3 × 5.
variables.match-a2.prompt: When a = 2, match each expression to its value.
variables.independent.b.fb: That is 2 × 3 only; do not forget +1.
solve-one-step.worked.prompt: In your own words: why divide both sides by 3?
solve-one-step.worked.fb: Right — dividing both sides keeps the balance and undoes the ×3.
solve-one-step.worked.content: 3x = 12: divide BOTH sides by 3 to get x = 4. Check: 3 × 4 = 12.
solve-one-step.order-solve.prompt: Put the steps for solving x ÷ 2 = 6 in order.
solve-one-step.order-solve.fb: Right: multiply both sides by 2, get x = 12, then check.
equation-balance.worked.prompt: In your own words: why do the same thing to both sides?
equation-balance.worked.fb: Right — doing the same to both sides keeps equality.
equation-balance.worked.content: x + 3 = 7 is a balance. Subtract 3 from BOTH sides: x = 4. Change one side only and it tips.
equation-balance.balance-choice.prompt: To solve x + 3 = 7, what keeps the balance?
equation-balance.match-solutions.prompt: Match each equation to its solution.
equation-balance.match-solutions.hint: Undo the operation on both sides.
solve-two-step.worked.prompt: In your own words: why subtract 5 before dividing by 2?
solve-two-step.worked.fb: Right — undo addition first, then multiplication (reverse order).
solve-two-step.worked.content: 2x + 5 = 13: subtract 5 from both sides (2x = 8), then divide by 2 (x = 4). Check: 2 × 4 + 5 = 13.
solve-two-step.solve.fb: Right: subtract 5 then divide by 2 gives 4.
solve-two-step.solve.scaffold: Subtract 5 from both sides: 13 − 5 = 8. Then divide by 2: 8 ÷ 2.
solve-two-step.order-solve.prompt: Put the steps for solving 3x − 4 = 11 in order.
solve-two-step.order-solve.fb: Right: add 4, get 3x=15, divide by 3, x=5.
word-to-equation.worked.prompt: In your own words: why is 2(x + 5) = 13 a different story?
word-to-equation.worked.fb: Right — 2(x+5) adds 5 first then doubles; the order differs.
word-to-equation.worked.hint: Follow the order of the words.
word-to-equation.worked.content: "A number doubled, plus 5, gives 13": doubled is 2x, plus 5 is +5, gives 13 → 2x + 5 = 13.
word-to-equation.which-eq.prompt: "A number doubled, plus 5, gives 13." Which equation?
word-to-equation.solve.scaffold: Subtract 5 from both sides, then divide by 2.
word-to-equation.match-stories.prompt: Match each story to its equation.
word-to-equation.match-stories.fb: Correct: the order of operations matches the words.
